_about: The game's glossary: the one list of fixed terms for every translation. scripts/i18n/i18n_tool.py reads it in `check` (the glossary gate on every translated line), `glossary` (this file's own checks, with the style guides in i18n/style/) and `weblate-glossary` (the TBX files uploaded to Weblate's glossary); nothing else lists these terms. Grown in PR L5 of the localization plan from the research trial's glossary (codex/localization-research at 520cad1, docs/research-2026-10/localization/pipeline/glossary.json: es-419, de, ja and ru for the first eight terms) to the 10 languages of decision D1, with decisions D9 (rephrase, never gender the engineer; names stored per language) and D11 (WOLF's voice and the key terms) at their defaults, approved by Nathanial on October 16, 2026. Every form here is a proposal for native reviewers (D8) and every final word is Nathanial's. Fields: 'languages' lists the glossary keys this file covers (the 'glossary' values of apps/game/i18n/languages.json for the 11 non-English files; Italian and Ukrainian are Tier 1 and not covered yet). 'inherit' maps a key that is an adaptation to its base: es-ES (Spain) uses es-419's form of every term that gives no es-ES form of its own. 'keep' lists the words copied through untranslated in every script (the script guard skips them). 'terms' is keyed by the English term: an all-capitals term (a station plate or a UI word) matches anywhere in an English line, any other term only as a whole word and only in that case ('breaker' does not match 'Breaker'). Each term has a 'note' (what it is and where it shows, for translators and Weblate) and per glossary key a form: 'status' is 'trial' (from the research trial), 'proposed' (written in L5, gated) or 'open' (a reviewer's word: not required yet); 'required' is the exact text a translation must contain whenever the English line has the term (null when open); 'variants' are other accepted forms (capitalised or inflected; for Slavic languages 'required' is a stem every case form contains); 'proposals' are candidates for an open term, shown to reviewers and never gated; 'avoid' are forms a translation of a line with the term must not contain (matched case-insensitively at the start of a word), each because a back-translation or decision D11 showed a wrong reading. 'names' holds the engineer's three provisional first names (D9; m0_state.gd) in the languages that write them in another script, as samples for reviewers, with Korean's particle class (the name's last sound picks 은/이 after a consonant, 는/가 after a vowel); Latin-script languages keep the English name. PR L7c moves the names into the game's own data and deletes them here, so there is never a second copy.

SAFE POINT.note: Station plate (12 px label) over the spot where the engineer is out of the sentry's sight; hints name it too. Plate words stay short.

TANK RELEASE.note: Station plate over the lever that drops a hanging coolant tank onto the floor below. Means drop or let go, never reset.

relay.note: An electrical relay on the base's power lines; a place the engineer and WOLF talk at, and the plate COOLANT RELAY.

bypass.note: A manual bypass that routes power or coolant around a fault; the plate MANUAL BYPASS.

sentry.note: The patrolling security robot (it). Never a person: no word for a human guard.

SENTRY.note: The sentry as an all-capitals word: the end card's recap topic (SENTRY, then two spaces).

coolant.note: The cooling fluid in the base's lines and the hanging tank; a released cloud of it is dangerous to cross. Not a soft drink: Brazilian Portuguese 'refrigerante' means soda.

the mark.note: The painted spot on the floor under the hanging tank, where WOLF draws the sentry.

breaker.note: A circuit breaker on a power line (decision D11). Not a light switch and not a weapon.

BREAKER.note: The breaker as a station plate (BREAKER, BREAKER LIVE, BREAKER TRIPPED, BREAKER USED, OVERLOAD BREAKER); use the same word as the hints (decision D3).

LOCKDOWN.note: The base sealing itself shut: the chapter name on the title (CHAPTER 1  /  LOCKDOWN) and a top card. Not a blockage or a lockout.

SERVICE JUNCTION.note: A room's name: the junction where the base's service lines (power and coolant) meet. A reviewer's word in every language (D11); the trial's German and Russian read back as 'supply node' and 'service node'.

Director.note: The Director, the person who runs the base (he/him). Written as a title used like a name; whether it is a title or a name is still open (D11), so Japanese 所長 ('head of the facility') stands for now and Korean and Chinese follow it.
